poi_mijas_cac.description: A permanent collection with original works by Picasso, Dalí and Miró, above all Picasso ceramics. Surprising for a village this size.
poi_mijas_cac.short_tip: About a 45-minute visit. A must, even if you're not into museums.

poi_mijas_plaza_toros.short_tip: One of the few square bullrings. It includes a small bullfighting museum.

poi_mijas_carromato.short_tip: A museum of oddities: the Last Supper on a grain of rice, or dressed fleas.

museo-historico.name: Historical and Ethnological Museum
museo-historico.description: In the old Town Hall, it recreates traditional life in Mijas: oil mill, wine cellar, kitchen, farm tools and the hideout where "the Mole of Mijas" lived for 30 years.
museo-historico.short_tip: A short visit for an almost symbolic price. On Plaza de la Libertad.

iglesia-inmaculada.name: Church of the Immaculate Conception
iglesia-inmaculada.description: A 16th-century church built over the old mosque, next to the town walls, with a tower of medieval origin.
iglesia-inmaculada.short_tip: Right behind it are the Muralla gardens and their views.

ermita-calvario.name: Calvario Hermitage
ermita-calvario.description: A small 18th-century hermitage on the hillside, reached by a pine-lined path with the Stations of the Cross. Views over the whole coast.
ermita-calvario.short_tip: About a 30-minute climb from the village. Bring water.

calle-san-sebastian.name: Calle San Sebastián
calle-san-sebastian.description: A steep street of whitewashed houses with flowerpots on the walls and the little San Sebastián chapel at the end. The most photographed spot in Mijas.
calle-san-sebastian.short_tip: Go early for photos without crowds.

donkey-dreamland.name: Donkey Dreamland
donkey-dreamland.description: A sanctuary that rescues abandoned or mistreated donkeys and mules. Volunteers show you around and tell each animal's story.
donkey-dreamland.short_tip: Free entry with a donation. Check visiting days before you go.

poi_mijas_burro_taxi.short_tip: Some visitors have concerns about the animals’ welfare: weigh it up before you ride.
